name: I2 — catalogue endpoint + prompt block + refs + linter
description:
Depends on I1 (client must already render cxj: links).

Spec: design/09-rich-links/README.md §6 (model instruction, 3 layers) and design/09-rich-links/richlinks.catalog.json — the catalog JSON already contains the literal `ai.emit` lines and the `promptBlock` template; it is the single source of truth and must not be duplicated by hand.

Do:
1. Move/serve the catalogue: API endpoint returning richlinks.catalog.json (version + kinds + actions), cached; client bundle and prompt builder both read the same source.
2. Prompt block injection: reuse the existing prompt assembly path (api/codx/junior/chat/chat_prompt_builder.py, api/codx/junior/autonomy/prompts.py, orchestration builders) — inject the generated promptBlock (grammar + emit rules + "never invent ids"), not a hardcoded copy.
3. `refs` in tool results: the 8 entity tools (task, chat, file, event, meet, message, profile, kanban card) return `refs: [{kind,id,label}]` so the model can copy real ids instead of hallucinating them.
4. Server-side linter: validate every `cxj:` occurrence in outgoing assistant text against the catalogue idPattern + existence check; strip/neutralise invalid ones; emit a `richlink_validity` metric.
5. Golden eval set: ~20 prompts whose expected output contains valid cxj: links; assert validity >= 0.9.

Acceptance:
- A real conversation produces links without the user asking for them.
- validity >= 0.9 on the golden set.
- A hallucinated id never reaches the UI (linter proof in the test).

Files: design/09-rich-links/*, api/codx/junior/chat/chat_prompt_builder.py, api/codx/junior/autonomy/prompts.py
